reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 3

samples_reviewed.question_text: Find the perimeter of the rectangle.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Find the perimeter of the rectangle.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Samples directly test 'Find the perimeter of the rectangle' and 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.', which together plausibly build toward the lc's pairing of identifying perimeter with using a measuring tool (ruler/cm).

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: perimeter (6 combos) and length_measurement (4 combos) are both registered for this node; my 5 samples are illustrative and exhaustive execution is handled by validate_matrix, not this review.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: 'Find the perimeter of the rectangle.' is a 6-word stem, well under the 18-word cap, and keeps the reading load light so cognitive effort goes toward the geometry/measurement task itself rather than parsing text.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The lc says 'using appropriate tools' but no sample text names or shows a tool (ruler, tape measure); the measuring items just state 'Measure the object' without an explicit tool reference, so that specific phrase in the competency is only weakly evidenced.

competency_alignment.rationale: Pairing perimeter-finding with plain length measurement is a sensible scope for 'identify and measure the perimeter', without overreaching into perimeter word-problems, which correctly belongs to the later lc mat_g2_mg_q4_6.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Observed perimeters (12, 18, 26) and lengths (9, 14 cm) are small, hand-computable numbers appropriate for grade 2 quarter 4 perimeter work without requiring large-number arithmetic.
